PlantForAdapt - Adapting planted forests with native species for resilient Amazonian territories in the face of global changes
PlantForAdapt is an international research collaboration between Brazil and France addressing key research priorities on native-species planted forests to support resilient Amazonian landscapes in the face of global change.
PlantForAdapt proposes an interdisciplinary scientific approach to tackle critical research priorities on planted forests in Amazonia. By placing strong emphasis on stakeholder engagement, PlantForAdapt will provide science-based guidelines to adapt management practices in tropical biodiverse planted forests to a rapidly changing context, while also contributing to cutting-edge scientific questions.
PlantForAdapt is led by Géraldine Derroire (PI, CIRAD and University of Brasilia), Romain Lehnebach (co-PI, CIRAD), Lucas Mazzei (co-PI, Embrapa) and Sylvain Schmitt (co-PI, CIRAD and INPA). Participating institutions are CIRAD (research units Forests and Societies, EcoFoG and Eco&Sols), Embrapa, INRAE, ONF (RDI of French Guiana) and its branches ONFi and ONF Brasil, University of French Guiana and University of Brasilia. It is funded by the foundation Velux Stiftung.

title: PlantForAdapt funded by Velux Stiftung
text:
We are delighted to announce that PlantForAdapt has been selected for funding by the Velux Stiftung under its 2026 Forestry call.






The Velux Stiftung is a Swiss philanthropic foundation that supports research and projects in areas such as forestry, with a focus on long-term, high-impact initiatives.
This funding will allow us to launch our international collaboration between Brazil and France on native-species planted forests, and to develop science-based guidelines for resilient Amazonian landscapes in the face of global change.
Stay tuned for more updates as the project gets underway!

title: PlantForAdapt
text: Amazonian forests, and their biodiversity and Nature Contribution to people, are increasingly threatened by deforestation, degradation and climate change. Brazil and French Guiana thus share the challenge of conserving and restoring their forests while promoting development, meeting an increasing timber demand and ensuring the well-being of their populations in a context where agricultural expansion and other land-use pressures also compete for forested land. Planted forests with native species represent an alternative to selective logging in natural forests and exotic species monocultures plantations, and can reconcile conservation of biodiversity with a diversified provision of wood products. In the face of climate change uncertainty, increasing diversity of planted species can improve planted forests resilience. However, the expansion of resilient and productive mixed forests with native species has thus far been constrained by critical knowledge gaps on tree species and the limited scientific basis for silvicultural guidelines, especially in a context of uncertainty related to their vulnerability to climate change. To ensure the resilience of planted forests to natural hazards, we thus crucially need the scientific basis for the selection of suitable candidate species within the immense diversity of native tree species, and the understanding of the effect of management practices on stand productivity and resilience. But this knowledge alone will not foster the adoption of plantations with native species unless it is confronted with the realities of the stakeholders likely to implement these practices. The success of this transformative change of practices therefore also depends on a solid understanding of the stakeholders’ perspectives.

title: PlantForAdapt
text:
Objectives
PlantForAdapt proposes a science-based interdisciplinary approach to tackle the gaps in knowledge on planted forests with native species and drive transformative changes in the management of these forests in Amazonia, aiming to enhance NCP in the face of climate uncertainties. It aims to study the potential of the high native tree biodiversity to propose innovative practices that can increase the resilience of planted forest to climate change and to provide a diversity of raw wood material and Nature Contribution to People. It will leverage long-term data from planted forests sites covering a diversity of practices and socio-environmental context, and analyse them through diverse modelling approaches to understand the dynamics of these forests. Through a strong involvement of key stakeholders throughout the project, PlantForAdapt will contribute to the adoption of forestry practices based on planted forests with natives species by tackling some of the critical research needs on the ecology of these forests, and identifying opportunities and potential additional barriers encountered by a diversity of stakeholders in two socio-economically contrasted contexts (Brazilian Amazon and French Guiana). The project will also foster transboundary collaboration between France (French Guiana) and Brazil, two territories sharing the same stake of promoting alternative and sustainable wood production practices in the face of climate change.

title: PlantForAdapt
text:
Scientific hypothesis
PlantForAdapt is based on the hypothesis that leveraging the high biodiversity of native tree species can enhance planted forest productivity and their resilience to climate change. Fostering species diversity in managed forests is a “no-regret approach” to climate-smart forestry, offering a scalable solution to ensure ecological functioning and NCP, including timber provision . Various mechanisms have been proposed to explain the effects of tree diversity on resource use and forest functioning, with consequences on tree, water and temperature stresses and wood production stability. More diverse forests can stabilises productivity by enhancing species asynchrony. In addition, biotic interactions between trees can improve forest productivity and resilience through resource partitioning and facilitation. However, beneficial effects of tree diversity may be overridden by competition in certain tree mixtures, especially during severe drought.

title: PlantForAdapt
text:
Project organisation


PlantForAdapt is organised around two biophysical work packages (WP1 and 2) and a third WP fostering stakeholder engagement. WP 1 will produce knowledge on native species potential for planted forests, and WP2 on the interest of mixed-species practices to increase planted forests resilience, two topics highlighted as critical research priorities for planted forests with native species 10,28 . By analysing stakeholder barriers and opportunities to adoption of planted forests with native species, WP3 will facilitate the co-design of practices grounded in stakeholders’ realities.
